# CopySync

> CopySync is a free, open-source (GNU AGPL-3.0) app for macOS, Windows and Linux that syncs the clipboard and files between computers: copy on one, paste on another, in any combination of Mac, Windows and Linux. It works across different accounts and different networks. On the same network no server is needed: devices find each other over mDNS and pair with a code. Across networks, a server the user hosts (or Tailscale) introduces them. Devices connect peer-to-peer over WebRTC with end-to-end DTLS encryption; when a direct connection fails, traffic is relayed through the user's TURN server. The server stores no accounts and cannot read clipboard content.
>
> CopySync 是一款免费开源（GNU AGPL-3.0）的 macOS、Windows 与 Linux 工具，在两台电脑之间同步剪贴板与文件：一台复制，另一台直接粘贴，Mac、Windows、Linux 互通。不要求同一个账号，跨网络可用。同一网络里不需要服务器，设备靠 mDNS 互相发现、用配对码配对；跨网络时由用户自建的服务器或 Tailscale 牵线。设备间 WebRTC 直连、DTLS 端到端加密，打不通时经用户服务器的 TURN 中转；服务器不存账号，看不到复制内容。

Key facts:

- Current version: 1.6.4, released 2026-10-13. On a Mac, the background service no longer leaks memory while it watches the clipboard (it grew by about 1 GB a day). 1.6.3: the Windows app ships the Visual C++ runtime it needs, so it starts on computers without the Visual C++ Redistributable. 1.6.2: the Windows installer runs on every Windows 10 version, not only 21H2 and later. 1.6.1: on a Mac, network discovery no longer restarts every minute or two while a paired computer is offline. 1.6.0 added the Linux client (x64 and ARM64, .deb and tar.gz), separate Mac downloads for Apple silicon and Intel, and a download page on the website. 1.5.0: Search nearby: open it on two computers on the same network and click the other one to pair without a code; a computer broadcasts its name only while the window is open. Windows now shows Chinese text in one consistent font. 1.4.0: computers on the same network pair and sync without a server (mDNS discovery, pairing code); on another subnet, enter the address shown under the pairing code; over Tailscale, enter the 100.x address. The server becomes optional and is only needed across networks. 1.3.4 added a quick start and step-by-step guides for the three ways to run the server (public server, LAN, LAN + Tailscale) on the website. 1.3.3: the server installs on Windows (as a service) and on a Mac (as a LaunchAgent) as well as Linux, and the website has a step-by-step guide for running it on a LAN. 1.3.2 stopped UU Remote placeholder files from looping through the history. 1.3.1: click a history item to preview images, including copied image files (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, BMP; HEIC and TIFF on Mac), with arrows to step through several. 1.3.0 added an English and Japanese interface (follows the system language, switchable in Settings) and moves to the GNU AGPL-3.0. 1.2.0 added the Windows client.
- Mac client: macOS 13 Ventura or later. Distributed as a DMG for Apple silicon (CopySync-mac-apple-silicon.dmg), one for Intel (CopySync-mac-intel.dmg), and a universal one (CopySync.dmg); not notarized by Apple, so the first launch needs "Open Anyway" in System Settings → Privacy & Security.
- Windows client: Windows 10 and Windows 11, x64. Per-user installer (CopySync-Setup.exe, no admin rights) or portable zip; not code-signed, so SmartScreen needs "More info → Run anyway" once. Runs in the notification area; pasted files are real files usable in Explorer, WeChat and Office. Skips content that password managers mark as sensitive.
- Linux client: x64 and ARM64, GTK 3; X11 desktops, or Wayland desktops with XWayland (GNOME and KDE include it by default). Tested on Ubuntu 24.04 GNOME. A .deb for Debian, Ubuntu and derivatives (installs to /opt/CopySync and adds a menu entry), or a tar.gz for other distributions (run install.sh to add a menu entry). The background service starts at login through an XDG autostart entry; data lives in ~/.local/share/copysync. No tray icon; reopen the window from the app menu. Skips content that password managers mark as sensitive.
- Local network mode (no server): devices on the same subnet find each other over mDNS (`_copysync._udp`, broadcasting only an anonymous token that changes daily) and exchange signed signaling over UDP 8788. On a different subnet, the user enters the address shown under the pairing code; addresses are remembered afterwards. Over Tailscale, the user enters the other computer's 100.x address when pairing. On Windows, Settings → Local network → Allow adds a firewall rule (one UAC prompt); on macOS 15, the background service needs the Local Network permission.
- Server (optional; only to sync across networks): a single static Go binary for Linux (x86_64, ARM64), macOS or Windows 10/11 x64. Install scripts register it as a systemd service (Linux), a LaunchAgent (macOS) or a Windows service with a firewall rule (Windows), and default to the machine's LAN address; Docker Compose also works on Linux. The three ways to connect are: the same network (no server), a public server (a cloud VM with a public IP; reachable from any network), or Tailscale (no server; pair by Tailscale address). A server on a LAN is still useful when two subnets can't reach each other. Ports: 8787/tcp (signaling), 3478/udp (STUN/TURN), plus OS-assigned UDP relay ports. In mainland China, cloud providers intercept plain HTTP (including the WebSocket handshake) for domains without an ICP filing, so clients should use the server's IP.
- Content synced: plain text, rich text (HTML plus a plain-text copy), images, files, folders.
- Works on multi-uplink networks (e.g. offices with two ISPs) that pick an uplink per destination: the client probes several STUN servers from one shared port to learn its address on every uplink and sends all of them to the peer. Diagnose with `copysync-cli nat`. If a connection lands on the relay first, the client retries the direct path with an ICE restart while idle.
- Items under 50 MB (adjustable 1 MB–1 GB) are pushed on copy; larger files sync as a record and are pulled on demand.
- History keeps 3 days by default (adjustable 1 hour–30 days).
- Pairing: 6-character code valid for 5 minutes (matched on the LAN, or through the server), plus a human check that both devices show the same two fingerprints (one per device's Ed25519 public key), which prevents man-in-the-middle attacks by the server.
- Not supported: iPhone/iPad (iOS forbids background clipboard monitoring). The server stores nothing: while the other computer is unreachable, the latest 20 items are kept in memory and sent when it reconnects (added to its history, not its clipboard).
- Compared with Apple's Universal Clipboard: no same-Apple-ID or proximity requirement, keeps a history, handles large files and folders.

## Docs

- [Website (English)](https://baiyuze.github.io/copysync/en/), [简体中文](https://baiyuze.github.io/copysync/), [日本語](https://baiyuze.github.io/copysync/ja/)
- [Quick start](https://baiyuze.github.io/copysync/en/start/): install the apps, pick a way to connect, and pair ([中文](https://baiyuze.github.io/copysync/start/), [日本語](https://baiyuze.github.io/copysync/ja/start/))
- [On the same network](https://baiyuze.github.io/copysync/en/lan/): no server; pairing across subnets, firewall and macOS permission notes ([中文](https://baiyuze.github.io/copysync/lan/), [日本語](https://baiyuze.github.io/copysync/ja/lan/))
- [Run the server on a public server](https://baiyuze.github.io/copysync/en/cloud/): security group, install script, checks ([中文](https://baiyuze.github.io/copysync/cloud/), [日本語](https://baiyuze.github.io/copysync/ja/cloud/))
- [Run the server on your LAN](https://baiyuze.github.io/copysync/en/server/): for subnets that can't reach each other; step-by-step guide for Windows, macOS and Linux ([中文](https://baiyuze.github.io/copysync/server/), [日本語](https://baiyuze.github.io/copysync/ja/server/))
- [Use it across networks with Tailscale](https://baiyuze.github.io/copysync/en/tailscale/): sync across networks with no server, pairing by Tailscale address ([中文](https://baiyuze.github.io/copysync/tailscale/), [日本語](https://baiyuze.github.io/copysync/ja/tailscale/))
- [Download](https://baiyuze.github.io/copysync/en/download/): every client package, with Mac builds for Apple silicon and Intel ([中文](https://baiyuze.github.io/copysync/download/), [日本語](https://baiyuze.github.io/copysync/ja/download/))
- [README (English)](https://github.com/baiyuze/copysync/blob/main/README.md): features and getting started ([中文](https://github.com/baiyuze/copysync/blob/main/README.zh-CN.md))
- [How it works](https://github.com/baiyuze/copysync/blob/main/guide/how-it-works.md): architecture, NAT traversal, security model, fallbacks, lessons learned
- [Troubleshooting](https://github.com/baiyuze/copysync/blob/main/guide/troubleshooting.md) and known limitations
- [Server deployment](https://github.com/baiyuze/copysync/blob/main/server/deploy/README.md): Windows, macOS, Linux (systemd), Docker and manual setup
- [Licensing](https://github.com/baiyuze/copysync/blob/main/LICENSING.md): AGPL-3.0 terms; versions 1.2.0 and earlier remain MIT
- [Windows client design (中文)](https://baiyuze.github.io/copysync/design/windows-client.html): clipboard formats, file-name compatibility, background process, installer
- [NAT traversal design (中文)](https://baiyuze.github.io/copysync/design/nat-traversal.html): multi-uplink probing, relay-to-direct upgrade, measurements and the NAT lab
- [Local network mode design (中文)](https://baiyuze.github.io/copysync/design/lan-mode.html): mDNS discovery, UDP signaling, pairing across subnets, Windows Firewall and macOS Local Network findings, NAT lab scenarios
- [Linux client design (中文)](https://baiyuze.github.io/copysync/design/linux-client.html): X11 clipboard over XWayland, INCR transfers, XDG autostart, packaging
- [Changelog](https://github.com/baiyuze/copysync/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
